articles.title: IAAPA Expo 2026 Sets Attendance Record with 39,000+ Attendees
articles.summary: IAAPA Expo 2026 was the largest in the event's history, drawing over 39,000 attendees and nearly 1,400 exhibiting companies across 634,000 square feet of exhibit space. The record-breaking show signals strong industry momentum and investment appetite heading into 2027. FEC operators should take note of the scale of innovation and supplier activity on display.

articles.title: IAAPA Expo 2026 Brass Ring Award Winners Announced
articles.summary: The 2026 Brass Ring Awards recognized the best exhibits and new products unveiled at IAAPA Expo 2026, among the industry's most prestigious honors. These awards highlight the suppliers and technologies gaining traction in the attractions and FEC space. Operators scouting new equipment or experiences should pay close attention to this year's winners.

articles.title: Zero Latency VR Opens Bookings for Jumanji: The Lost Levels
articles.summary: Zero Latency VR has launched ticket sales for Jumanji: The Lost Levels, a free-roam VR experience available at its venues worldwide from December 4, 2026. The experience is the first from Zero Latency to feature fully hand-tracked gameplay, eliminating controllers and making it accessible to guests of all ages. FEC operators with VR attractions should monitor this IP-driven, family-friendly product as a benchmark for next-generation guest engagement.

articles.title: Zero Latency Launches Jumanji VR Experience with Full Hand Tracking
articles.summary: Zero Latency VR's new Jumanji: The Lost Levels experience goes live at global venues December 4, 2026, featuring fully hand-tracked gameplay for the first time in the company's history. The family-focused format — designed for guests aged eight to eighty — broadens the demographic appeal of free-roam VR beyond core gamers. This represents a significant step toward making location-based VR a mainstream FEC anchor attraction.

articles.title: Triotech Unveils Five New Products at IAAPA Expo 2026 in Largest-Ever Release
articles.summary: Immersive attraction manufacturer Triotech debuted five new products at IAAPA Expo 2026, marking the largest single product launch in the company's history. The breadth of new offerings signals aggressive expansion in the interactive and immersive ride market relevant to FECs and entertainment venues. Operators evaluating new anchor attractions should track Triotech's expanded lineup.

articles.title: Alterface Debuts Ultra-Low Latency Interactive Technology at IAAPA Expo 2026
articles.summary: Alterface showcased a new interactive shooting system at IAAPA Expo 2026 featuring 30-millisecond latency and high-precision tracking, giving designers greater creative freedom while delivering highly responsive guest interactions. The technology is directly applicable to FEC dark ride and interactive attraction installations. Operators planning interactive experience upgrades should evaluate this system's precision and design flexibility.

articles.title: Slick City 'Dry Waterpark' FEC Opens in Schererville, Indiana
articles.summary: Slick City has opened a new family entertainment center in Schererville, Indiana, expanding its dry waterpark concept that replaces water with synthetic sliding surfaces. The brand continues to grow rapidly, with additional locations also announced for San Antonio and Boise, demonstrating strong franchising momentum. FEC operators and investors should watch Slick City as a disruptive indoor attraction format attracting significant consumer interest.

articles.title: Slick City Action Park to Open New San Antonio Location
articles.summary: Slick City Action Park has announced a new location coming to San Antonio, continuing the brand's rapid national expansion of its indoor dry slide concept. The chain's growth across multiple major markets highlights rising consumer demand for novel indoor active-entertainment formats. FEC operators in those markets should assess competitive implications as Slick City scales.

articles.title: Slick City Expands Further with New Boise Location
articles.summary: Slick City is set to open a location on Milwaukee Street in Boise, adding to its growing roster of dry waterpark FEC venues nationwide. The brand's simultaneous expansion into Schererville, San Antonio, and Boise underscores its aggressive growth strategy. This chain's trajectory makes it one of the most-watched emerging FEC concepts for operators and investors alike.

articles.title: Xola Booking Platform Expands Focus on Escape Rooms, VR, and Indoor Attractions
articles.summary: Xola, an online booking and operations platform founded in 2011, serves a broad range of FEC-adjacent operators including escape rooms, VR attractions, and indoor experiences. The platform offers real-time reservation management, multi-channel ticketing, POS, and marketing tools through a single interface. Operators looking to streamline front-of-house operations and OTA distribution should evaluate Xola as a purpose-built solution for their sector.

articles.title: EAG360 Announces Speaker Lineup for January Seminar Programme
articles.summary: EAG360, a key trade event for the coin-op, amusement, and gaming industries, has published its seminar programme for January, featuring speakers from Euromat, Hippodrome Casino, and other senior industry figures. The integrated seminar-and-exhibition format is designed to deliver actionable insights for amusement and FEC operators. Operators active in the UK and European arcade and amusement sector should consider attending.

articles.title: Woozone to Exhibit Trampoline Park and Indoor Playground Equipment at IAAPA Expo Europe 2027
articles.summary: Chinese manufacturer Woozone will showcase its indoor playground and trampoline park equipment at IAAPA Expo Europe 2027 in Vienna, September 21–23. The company designs, manufactures, and installs equipment for a range of FEC environments. Operators planning facility buildouts or equipment refreshes should note Woozone's presence for sourcing opportunities.

articles.title: ProSlide Commits $15 Million R&D Investment in Next-Generation Water Ride Technology
articles.summary: ProSlide Technology is investing $15 million in research and development focused on water coaster technology, PowerRAPIDS river systems, and immersive water slide innovations. While primarily relevant to waterpark operators, the immersive technology developments may crossover to hybrid FEC environments combining wet and dry attractions. The investment signals that major suppliers are prioritizing experiential differentiation through technology.

articles.title: Elev8 Fun Overhauling Attractions at Seminole Towne Center FEC
articles.summary: Elev8 Fun is undertaking a major overhaul of its attractions at the Seminole Towne Center location, refreshing the guest experience at the mall-based FEC. Attraction refreshes are a key strategy for FECs to retain repeat visitors and compete with new entrants in their markets. The move illustrates the growing importance of continuous capital reinvestment for FEC operators in retail-adjacent settings.

articles.title: Rethinking Retail Strategy in Amusement Parks: Put Product Where Guests Need It
articles.summary: A Kiosk Marketplace analysis examines how amusement and entertainment venues can boost retail revenue by repositioning merchandise and F&B offerings closer to guest decision-making moments. The strategic placement of kiosks and retail touchpoints is increasingly relevant as FECs look to grow ancillary revenue beyond ticket sales. Operators should review their current floor layouts through the lens of guest journey mapping.

articles.title: AI Recommendation Engine for Live Venues Personalizes the Guest Journey
articles.summary: A new recommendation engine for venue apps moves beyond static directories to serve each guest a single personalized 'best next activity' suggestion, drawing on queue times, party composition, and schedule data. Research across nine venues found that 33–59% of point-of-interest discovery occurred through just three app screens, highlighting how much guidance guests actually want. FEC operators with mobile apps should explore how personalization algorithms can reduce guest indecision and increase attraction utilization.

articles.title: Texas FEC AR's Entertainment Hub Closes Abruptly After Six Years
articles.summary: AR's Entertainment Hub in Baytown, Texas, has abruptly shuttered after nearly six years of operation, leaving guests and local families without a go-to indoor entertainment destination. Sudden closures of this type are a cautionary signal for FEC operators about the importance of financial planning and community communication. The closure also creates a potential market gap in the Baytown area for competitors or new entrants.

articles.title: UK's First Human Claw Machine Opens in Leicester as Indoor Entertainment Hub Grows
articles.summary: Leicester has launched the UK's first human claw machine attraction as part of a broader indoor entertainment cluster developing in the city centre. The novelty concept — where guests are lowered into a giant prize-filled arena — illustrates the ongoing appetite for shareable, social-media-friendly FEC experiences. Operators looking to differentiate their offering with low-footprint, high-buzz activations should take note.

articles.title: Omaha Property Eyed for Conversion to Indoor Entertainment Venue
articles.summary: A commercial property at 3002 Dodge Street in Omaha is being considered for redevelopment as an indoor entertainment venue. The conversion of underutilized retail or commercial real estate into FEC space is a growing national trend as landlords seek experiential tenants. This story is a useful reference point for operators or investors exploring opportunistic real estate plays in secondary markets.

articles.title: Four Lake Houston Entertainment Venues Share Operational Updates
articles.summary: Four entertainment venues in the Lake Houston area have provided updates on their operations, expansions, and offerings. Regional roundups like this reflect the density of FEC activity in suburban Texas markets and the competitive landscape operators face. FEC professionals tracking market activity in the Houston metro should follow developments in this cluster.

articles.title: Mississippi Entertainment Development 'The Gallery' Wins TIF Approval
articles.summary: A mixed-use development called 'The Gallery' in Madison County, Mississippi, has received Tax Increment Financing plan approval, potentially including family entertainment components. TIF-backed entertainment developments are an increasingly common funding mechanism for new FEC-anchored retail projects across the South. Operators and developers scouting sites in the region should monitor this project's progress.

articles.title: Madison County Approves $11.7 Million TIF Borrowing for Retail and Dining Development
articles.summary: Madison County, Mississippi, has approved up to $11.741 million in Tax Increment Financing borrowing to support a new retail and dining development that may include entertainment uses. Public financing tools like TIF are increasingly being used to attract FEC and entertainment tenants to mixed-use developments. FEC developers and operators should track how municipalities are using incentives to attract experiential tenants.

articles.title: Rethinking Experience Design: Why Siloed Teams Undermine FEC and Attraction Projects
articles.summary: An industry commentary argues that the traditional separation of architecture, interiors, creative development, and engineering into distinct silos routinely undermines the success of entertainment and hospitality projects. The piece calls for integrated, interdisciplinary project structures that prioritize the overall experience outcome rather than individual discipline performance. FEC operators undertaking facility design or renovation should use this framework when structuring their design and build teams.

articles.title: AV Industry Faces 2.3 Million Professional Shortfall — a Risk for Attraction Operators
articles.summary: The global AV industry faces a shortage of over 2.3 million professionals, creating real risks of project delays and operational resilience issues for attractions relying on sophisticated audiovisual technology. Women represent only 9% of the commercial AV workforce, compounding the pipeline problem. FEC operators dependent on AV-driven experiences — projection mapping, interactive walls, immersive shows — should factor talent scarcity into project planning and vendor selection.

articles.title: Querion Hypermedia Entertainment Park Concept Profiled
articles.summary: Blooloop has profiled Querion, a hypermedia entertainment park concept that blends physical and digital experiences in a novel format. Emerging hybrid experience formats like Querion represent the leading edge of what FEC operators may compete with or draw inspiration from in the coming years. Operators focused on innovation and next-generation guest experience design should explore this concept.

articles.title: Brogent Technologies Partners with United Parks, Sony, and Toho on New Flying Theater Attractions
articles.summary: Brogent Technologies has announced partnerships with United Parks, Grupo Iter, Sony, and Toho to deliver new immersive flying theater experiences globally. The collaborations expand Brogent's footprint and validate the continued demand for large-format flying ride attractions in parks and entertainment venues. FEC operators with sufficient footprint evaluating premium anchor attractions should follow Brogent's growing portfolio.

articles.title: Shooting Near Baton Rouge Chuck E. Cheese Raises Safety Concerns for FECs
articles.summary: A man was injured in a shooting near a Chuck E. Cheese in Baton Rouge following an altercation that began inside the venue, drawing renewed attention to safety and security protocols at family entertainment centers. The incident underscores the importance of robust incident response plans, trained staff, and venue security measures for FEC operators. Operators should review their safety policies and consider physical security upgrades in light of incidents like this.

articles.title: Amusement Today December 2026 Issue Now Available
articles.summary: The December 2026 issue of Amusement Today, a leading trade publication covering the amusement and attractions industry, is now available for readers. The issue likely covers IAAPA Expo 2026 highlights, new product launches, and year-end industry trends. FEC operators and suppliers should consult this issue for a comprehensive recap of the industry's biggest month.
